result.summary: The image shows a well-developed urban commercial environment with wide, paved sidewalks and signalized intersections. Pedestrian safety is supported by clear signals and 'No Turn on Red' signage, though the crossing distance is unprotected by physical medians.

hazards.description: The parallel line crosswalk markings are less visible to approaching motorists than high-visibility patterns.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade existing parallel line markings to continental or ladder style markings to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

result.summary: The image shows a dense urban commercial street with wide, well-maintained sidewalks and curb ramps. However, there is a lack of marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals at the immediate corner, which may increase risk during crossings.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, which fails to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians and does not define a clear path for crossing.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb may obstruct the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street where cars are parked

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to increase visibility and define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals, providing a clear path for walkers. However, the multi-lane roadway and presence of vehicles stopped close to the crossing create potential sightline issues and exposure risks.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Stopped Vehicles
hazards.description: The white vehicle stopped near the crosswalk on the right side of the image may obstruct the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking or stopping spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

result.summary: This is a high-density urban intersection with significant pedestrian activity and commercial land use. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and pedestrian signals are present, the environment is degraded by faded crosswalk markings and poor pavement quality.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk lines are significantly worn, making the pedestrian crossing area less visible to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground across the roadway

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The roadway surface is cracked and uneven, presenting potential tripping hazards for pedestrians and affecting vehicle control.
